_comment: Copy to zfs-hold-tight.json (kept next to the binary, or point at it with ZFS_HOLD_TIGHT_CONFIG) and edit for your pool. The real config is git-ignored.
_comment_namespace: Prefix for this tool's ZFS user-properties and hold tags (<ns>:keep_until, <ns>:tier, <ns>:monthly, <ns>:adhoc). Defaults to 'zht'. If migrating from a build that used another prefix, set it to the old value to keep managing existing holds.
_comment_zfsPath: Absolute path to the zfs binary. Omit to auto-resolve (/usr/sbin/zfs, /sbin/zfs, ...); set explicitly to avoid trusting the root cron's PATH. curlPath is the same for curl (healthchecks only).
_comment_healthchecks: Optional. A healthchecks.io (or compatible) base ping URL. Leave unset (or pass --no-hc) to disable pings entirely. zfs-hold-tight pings the base URL on a clean prune and <url>/fail with diagnostics on any HOLD or destroy failure.
_comment_min_newer_holds: Two-holds INVARIANT: a plain daily is destroyed only once at least this many HELD keepers (weekly/monthly grandfathers) are strictly newer than it, AND it is older than dailyKeepDays (below). Default 3 (was 2): a held keeper only ever advances into the 2nd-newest slot when an ISO-week closes, so at minNewerHolds=2 a whole week's worth of plain dailies sit at 'exactly 1 newer hold' simultaneously and cross to 'doomed' together the instant the next week's keeper appears -- one more required hold buys a full extra week of buffer before that batch can trigger. GLOBAL DEFAULT; overridable per retention policy.
_comment_guards: These are the GLOBAL DEFAULTS. Each guard is evaluated INDEPENDENTLY per dataset (a small dataset's deletion/encryption is flagged on its own scale). Any guard key may also be set inside a retention policy to override the default for that group of datasets.
_comment_shrink: HOLD + alert when the newest daily references this many % less data than the recent baseline median — catches mass DELETION. 0 disables.
_comment_churn: HOLD + alert when the newest daily rewrites more than this % of the dataset's referenced data — catches mass REWRITE / in-place ENCRYPTION. 0 disables.

baseline._comment: general datasets - two-holds daily tail, 5 years of weeklies/monthlies. dailyKeepDays is a real calendar FLOOR: a plain daily survives at least this long regardless of hold coverage, bounding how much daily-granularity history one ISO-week close can collapse in a single run.

low._comment: bulk/media - write-once, so tighten the content guards (any change is suspicious). A shorter daily floor here (7d) than baseline (30d), since media churns less and the size makes long daily retention costlier.

volatile._comment: scratch/churny datasets - data changes a lot by design, so relax/disable churn
